title: Response Anomaly Catalog & Quick Hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal catalog of weird outputs I keep hitting during ad-hoc sampling runs. Not formalized — meant to capture reproducible examples, quick severity rubric, immediate hypotheses, and experiments to run before escalating to the runtime/quantization owners.

TL;DR (one-liner):
- Frequent small hallucinations (dates, short citations) across mid-length prompts; occasional format drift that breaks function-calling JSON outputs; rare truncation where response cuts mid-sentence; intermittent repetition loops for long multi-turn queries.

Observed categories (taxonomy):
1) Micro-hallucination: short factual mismatches (years, city names, citations) that are plausible but wrong. Severity: 2-3/5. Frequency: medium.
2) Structured-format drift: model used to return perfectly-formed JSON for tool-call outputs; now some responses include trailing commas, missing keys, or stray text outside the JSON block. Severity: 3/5 for downstream consumers. Frequency: medium-low.
3) Abrupt truncation: output stops after "...and the next step is" or mid-CSV row. Severity: 3-4/5 for flows relying on full output. Frequency: rare.
4) Repetition loop: model starts repeating a short phrase or sentence 3-10x near end of response (observed in >2048 token histories). Severity: 2-4/5 depending on consumer. Frequency: low but high-impact for long chat sessions.
5) Safety over-blocking / token drop: in a few prompts the model replaces expected content with "[REDACTED]" or produces empty answers for benign prompts — possible filter false-positives. Severity: 3/5. Frequency: low.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (quick):
- Severity (impact to product): 1 (cosmetic) - 5 (breaks pipeline)
- Reproducibility: "easy" (deterministic w/seed), "flicker" (sometimes), "hard" (rare stochastic)
- Suggested owner: runtime | quantization | routing | model-onboard

Representative examples (copied from quick runs):
1) Prompt: "Give me a short citation for the 2018 Redwood Inference latency paper."
   Output: "Redwood, J. (2018). Low-latency inference. Proceedings of the Cloud ML Conf, pp. 45-49."
   Annotation: invented citation (micro-hallucination). Reproducibility: easy with model v1.4-quant; seed 42. Owner: model-onboard / eval.

2) Prompt: function-call style (system: return only JSON)
   Output: "{\n    \"completion\": \"42\",\n    \"metadata\": {\"time_ms\": 132}\n   }, unexpected tail text"
   Annotation: stray text after JSON -> JSON parser crash in ingestion. Reproducible with v1.5-quant on short-context runs. Owner: runtime (formatting / streaming boundary).

3) Prompt: long multi-turn agent conversation (approx 6k tokens history)
   Output: repeats: "We should check the dataset." x7 and then ends.
   Annotation: repetition loop at high context lengths. Reproducibility: flicker; more likely when batch load is high. Owner: serving-runtime / kv-cache logic.

4) Prompt: "List the steps to reset the appliance and include the diagnostic code:"
   Output: "[REDACTED]"
   Annotation: safety filter triggered incorrectly for benign admin instruction. Reproducibility: hard but seen in prod 2x last week. Owner: safety / content-filter config.

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Quantization kernel change (recent PR in runtime) introduced subtle tokenization/rounding artifacts that increase improbable token probabilities -> micro-hallucinations and format corruption. (owner: quantization/serving-runtime)
- H2: Streaming boundary bug where final stream flush not synchronized with JSON closing brace -> stray trailing text. (owner: serving-runtime/streaming)
- H3: KV-cache eviction at >4096 context boundary causes repetition loop because decoder state not fully cleared/rotated. (owner: serving-runtime/cache)
- H4: New safety heuristics upstream tuned too aggressively (false positives) for certain phrasing patterns -> overblocking. (owner: safety squad / eval)
- H5: Model routing fallback to small-lm variant under heavy load leads to format mismatch (small-lm doesn't honor system prompt strictly). (owner: routing/orchestration)

Quick experiments to run (PRIORITY order):
- E1: Re-run failing samples with pinned older kernel (tag: runtime@v1.5.2) and quant disabled (or use fp16 path). Measure micro-hallucination delta. (Expected: if quant is cause, behavior improves).
- E2: Replay same prompt with streaming disabled (complete output at once) to see if trailing text persists.
- E3: Run long-history conversation with KV-cache off (or small ctx chunking) to check repetition frequency.
- E4: Re-evaluate safety filter logs for redacted prompts; collect token-level scoring to see why redaction triggered.
- E5: Force routing to hosted-high-capacity model (no fallback) for one hour and monitor format errors.

Quick experiment notes (done so far):
- Ran E1 for 10 samples: pin to runtime@v1.5.1 reduced JSON format tails in 9/10 cases, but not all micro-hallucinations. Suggests streaming/buffer fix in 1.5.1.
- Ran E3 with KV-cache disabled on one host: repetition loop frequency dropped from 6% -> 1.2% on that host (small sample). Promising.

Immediate mitigation steps (short-term):
- Add parser guard: tolerate trailing text after JSON with a small regex extractor for first JSON object (stopgap).
- For mission-critical flows, add model pinning option to avoid fallback routing until root cause fixed.
- Add targeted unit test in regression harness covering the JSON streaming edge case and repetition with >4k token history.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Are there recent kernel/quant PRs that changed token-level emission order? Need diff of PRs last 6 weeks and perf tests. (Action: @Priya to pull PR list)
- Q: Does the safety filter share a common signature with earlier false-positive cases? (Action: @Ethan inspect filter logs and thresholds)
- Add systematic coverage: create 200 prompt mini-suite with structured outputs + long-context chats to run nightly.

Notes to self (todo list):
- Create Linear ticket with reproducible minimal example + seed for the micro-hallucination case.
- Draft short Slack message to runtime team with experiment logs and ask for quick triage.
- Add this doc to Confluence under "QA: output drift 2026" after clean up.

Random stray observations (hand notes):
- Some format drift seems correlated with token-limit warnings in logs ("truncation-warning" at 1:23am) — maybe streaming flush is tied to token-limit path.
- When we force temperature=0 (greedy), hallucinations reduce marginally but some structure issues remain -> likely not purely sampling related.
- Several consumer bugs surfaced only because parser died on trailing text; short-term guard + more tolerant parser should reduce incident noise.

Contact / follow ups:
- Priya (applied-ml) — owns regression harness and can add tests.
- Ethan (runtime) — owns streaming/kv-cache changes.

End of doc — rough draft. Will tidy if triage shows a single root cause.

-- Luca
